items.quote: Two clubs will share the invitation.
items.note: Stated commitment to share; reach, not sign-ups.

items.quote: Reach is not the same as successful matches.
Students trade short skill sessions - design for coding, music for maths - and learn from each other.

opening.framing: A hand-run skill swap inside one club, for students with a live project need who can give one skill back later, not necessarily to the same person.

claims.text: Some students with a live project need would give an hour of their own skill in return for help.
Two clubs sharing the invitation gives enough reach to hand-match a first small group without building an app.
A hand-run trial is a cheap, reversible community experiment, which is what the goal asks for.

assumptions: Students attend sessions they sign up for.
Helpers accept one-way help at first.
outside_view: Peer tutoring: help is wanted, helpers are scarce.
Time banks: early enthusiasm, then drop-off.
opening.concession: Club reach shows distribution, not demand. Nothing on record shows a matched pair meeting yet.

proving_test.action: Collect one skill to offer and one goal from each participant in one club; hand-match ten pairs.
proving_test.metric: Pairs completing at least one session; helpers saying they would help again
proving_test.success_threshold: At least 6 of 10 pairs complete a session

opening.statement: Every campus has people who can teach something and want to learn something else. Start small: one club, matches made by hand, help that can be paid forward. The clubs can reach people; what we don't know is whether pairs actually meet. So make ten matches and count the sessions that happen.
